accepted_gaps.because: Sole operator on this repository (Sven, 2026-09-11: 'do not protect main. i am the only operator on these repos, and the goal of the framework i use is to ensure proper discipline'). Protection was deleted on 2026-09-12 with that instruction restated. What it was costing: `strict` made every merge leave every other open pull request BEHIND, so each landing charged the next one a fresh ~15-minute `unittest` re-run against a base that had moved for no reason the diff cared about, and a queue of six could not be landed in a day. What it was buying was already unbuyable here -- a review requirement on the one account that merges means self-approval, which GitHub forbids, and `enforce_admins` gated nobody but the sole admin. What is genuinely lost is the server-side backstop on a red merge, and what stands in for it is named rather than assumed: the maintainer reads every check on the pull request before `gh pr merge`, one person and not a gate. `sd-ship merge` is not the replacement while this gap stands: it reads the protection object before the pull request's checks and refuses a missing one (bin/sd_ship_remote.py, protection()), so it becomes runnable again only when protection returns.
accepted_gaps.until: a second account with push or merge rights on this repository exists
